correctness.rationale: Two independently designed executable exact algorithms reconstruct all first 3101 squarefree seven-prime products; a complete zero-one subset-sum bitset for the first 3100 over 0..40000000 has largest missing value 19027139. The next unused coin is 19114095 and the certified interval above the gap has length 20972861. Bertrand implies c_(j+1)<2c_j, so consecutive shifted covered intervals overlap at every further coin. Since c_3100>19027139, later coins cannot fill the gap. All quantifiers and finite-to-infinite steps are explicit.

value.rationale: Butler, Erdős and Graham proposed determination of the exact a(k) conductors and published only a(1)..a(6). This computes the first missing natural exact invariant a(7), with a certified infinite boundary, furnishing quantitative understanding of the smallest obstruction and onset of permanent coverage in an established prime-product subset-sum construction. It is not an arbitrary cutoff or a known-table recomputation.
